title: The geometric stalk evaluation homomorphism on units is bijective
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $K^{sep}$ its separable closure, $\Omega$ its algebraic closure, $p$ its geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and $\mathbb G_m$ its units sheaf [def-sc-gm-torsor]. Suppose an additive homomorphism $f:(\mathbb G_m)_p\to (K^{sep})^\times$ [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology] satisfies the evaluation formula on every unit germ: its image embedded into $\Omega$ is the value of the representing unit at the geometric lift. Then $f$ is bijective. This conclusion has no Galois action or equivariance clause.

proof.text: For surjectivity, a separable-closure unit and its inverse belong to a finite separable subextension. Its spectrum is an etale K-neighbourhood and its inclusion in the algebraic closure gives a lift. The corresponding unit germ maps to the original unit by the evaluation formula and injectivity of the separable-closure embedding.

For injectivity, represent both elements by germs. Refine their neighbourhoods to connected affine components at the chosen lift, each the spectrum of a finite separable field extension. Embed both fields into the algebraic closure using the lifts and take their finite separable compositum. It gives a common pointed etale refinement. Equality of evaluations makes the pulled-back units equal in the compositum, so the original germs agree in the stalk colimit. The argument includes imperfect fields and uses only separable extensions.
